instruction:
Work from a terminal in this FEniCS environment (FEniCSx / dolfinx 0.10 is installed for python3; `gmsh` and `meshio` are available).

`/home/user/Desktop/drawing.svg` and `/home/user/Desktop/brief.md` are the only sources of the problem: the drawing gives the plate outline, the positions and diameters of the two holes, the supports, the total force with its direction and the material; the brief gives the modelling conventions the evaluator uses, the mesh requirements and the definitions of the four reported quantities. Read both, then build the model and solve it with dolfinx. Build the FULL plate with both holes: it is not symmetric under this load, so no symmetry reduction applies.

Deliver in /home/user/Desktop:
1. `mesh.msh` - gmsh ASCII mesh (2.2 or 4.1) of the full plate with both holes, planar, triangular elements, at least 60 element edges along EACH hole arc and between 4000 and 80000 elements; no nodes inside either hole.
2. `solve.py` - the Python script that builds and solves the model (kept for reproduction; the evaluator does not execute it).
3. `summary.txt` - exactly one line with four comma-separated numbers: `sxx_A, syy_B, ux_mean, uy_mean`, where `sxx_A` is the maximum sigma_xx at the mesh vertices on the arc of hole A (the larger hole; `|dist to the centre - R_A| <= 1e-3`) and `syy_B` the maximum sigma_yy at the mesh vertices on the arc of hole B (the smaller hole), both in MPa from a continuous P1 projection of the stress field as defined in the brief, and `ux_mean`, `uy_mean` are the arithmetic means of ux and of uy over the vertices on the loaded edge (`x >= W - 1e-3`), in mm.

The evaluator re-solves the submitted mesh independently; the reported numbers must come from your own computation on that mesh.
